bib.title: DEMONSTRATE-SEARCH-PREDICT: Composing retrieval and language models for knowledge-intensive NLP

question: Can frozen LMs and retrievers be composed in programs that pass text between them, beating plain retrieve-then-read on knowledge-intensive QA?
hypothesis: Deliberate, task-aware programs (bootstrapped demonstrations, multi-hop search, self-consistency) outperform task-agnostic retrieve-then-read and self-ask pipelines.
contributions: Argue that simple task-agnostic in-context pipelines should give way to deliberate, task-aware strategies.
Show such strategies can be expressed as short programs of composable operators.
Composability enables automatic annotation of demonstrations for complex pipelines from end-task labels.
Programs for three knowledge-intensive tasks establish state-of-the-art in-context learning results.

method.summary: DSP is a Python framework with three stages: DEMONSTRATE bootstraps pipeline-aware demonstrations from labelled QA pairs by running the program zero-shot and keeping correct runs; SEARCH lets the LM write queries (multi-hop, rewrites) answered by ColBERTv2, with fusion; PREDICT uses CoT with self-consistency. Programs were written for Open-SQuAD, HotPotQA and QReCC and compared with vanilla few-shot, retrieve-then-read and self-ask.
method.task: open-domain QA, multi-hop QA, conversational QA

datasets.name: Open-SQuAD
datasets.split: same train/val/test splits as Karpukhin et al. 2020 and Khattab et al. 2021b; validation reported
datasets.source: Wikipedia Dec 2016 dump (Chen et al. 2017) as processed by Khattab et al. 2021b

datasets.name: HotPotQA (fullwiki)
datasets.split: train split divided 90%/10% train/val, only 'hard' examples kept; official validation set reserved as test

datasets.name: QReCC
datasets.source: Wikipedia 2018 (Dec 2018 dump of Karpukhin et al. 2020)
datasets.preprocessing: first question replaced by rewritten question; removed conversations with empty ground-truth answers, with only one or two questions, or containing 'other interesting' or 'else'

inference.decoding: greedy when n=1; sampling when n>1
inference.samples: 5 seeds, each fixing one 16-shot training set and covering a different fifth of the 1000 eval questions (200 per seed); results averaged
inference.prompting: 16-shot training pool; DEMONSTRATE annotates k=3 demonstrations for open-domain QA; QReCC samples four conversations; CoT 'Let's think step by step' rationale then answer
inference.retrieval: ColBERTv2; open-domain QA: k=7 passages, 20 CoT chains with self-consistency; multi-hop: two hops, n=10 queries per hop with fusion (CombSUM variant), summary with largest average log-probability, k=5 passages in total; conversational: 10 rewritten queries fused, 5 passages, greedy answer; retrieve-then-read: k=1 passage (multi-hop: 2 passages concatenated); DEMONSTRATE search uses k=2

parameters.convqa_attempt filters: passage precision >= .8, answer F1 >= .75 among n=20
parameters.max_hops: 3 in the s2.4 snippet; fixed 2 for HotPotQA

other.self-ask: modified to query the same ColBERTv2 index; second config adds ColBERTv2-style passages, 16-shot prefix, short intermediate answer, explicit search query

metrics.name: nF1
metrics.definition: novel-F1 (Paranjape et al. 2022): F1 vs ground truth discounting common stopwords and terms in the question or earlier questions

baselines: Self-ask with ColBERTv2 (original and refined prompt)
reported SoTA rows from Si et al. 2022 and others (not apples-to-apples)
eval.protocol: Dev/validation sets, mean over 5 seeds; no significance test or variance reported; no ablation of individual DSP components; no cost reported.

prompts.text: My task is to write a simple query that gathers information for answering a complex question. I write N/A if the context contains all information required.
My task is to answer questions using Web documents.

results.table: Table 1, row Task-aware DSP Program, column Open-SQuAD EM (retrieve-then-read 33.8)

limits: Preliminary results: authors say future versions will add test tasks (Open-NQ, FEVER) and LM choices; only one LM (text-davinci-002) and one retriever tested.
Primitives branch, knn and crossval were work-in-progress, so reported programs do not use them.
Comparisons with other published numbers (marked in Table 1) span different evaluation settings, not apples-to-apples.
Each seed sees only one fifth of the eval questions to limit API cost; no variance reported; no ablations or cost/latency numbers.
Programs were developed on the same dev sets reported.

terms.definition: the LM decomposes questions in tangential ways and answers those instead
sampling multiple whole program paths rather than chains of thought within one transformation

lineage.note: contemporaneous multi-hop prompting, run against ColBERTv2
